newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech refinery sees fire damage at CZK 230-250mln.
newsitem.headline: Czech refinery sees fire damage at CZK 230-250mln.

text.p: The main Czech refinery, Ceska Rafinerska a.s., said on Friday that last November's fire at its tanking site caused damage estimated at 230-250 million crowns ($7.5-$8.2 million).
The company is 49 percent owned by a consortium of Royal Dutch/Shell, Du Pont de Nemours' unit Conoco, and Italy's Agip SpA.
"We estimate the damage at 230 to 250 million crowns," Rafinerska's General Director Ivan Ottis told a news conference.
"Two hundred million is the cost of reconstruction, while the rest is the damage to materials and fire extinguishing costs," he said, adding that appraisal of the accident was still under way.
Ottis said the tanking terminal and petrol mixing unit, also hit by the fire, should be completely reconstructed by the end of the year.
The two-day fire broke out at Rafinerska's Litvinov refinery on November 23 last year, and interrupted production and supplies to neighbouring chemicals plant Chemopetrol for several days.
A second fire just eight days later damaged Rafinerska's hydrocracking unit at the same site, forcing the company to shut it down for several weeks.

Rafinerska a.s. said last week that it posted an audited gross profit of 1.172 billion crowns for 1996, its first year of full operation, on sales of 36.629 billion crowns. The company said this year's profits would be higher but gave no precise forecasts.
Its gross profit for the first three months of this year was 427 million.
Rafinerska was established with the merger of the refining operations of petrochemical firms Chemopetrol Group a.s. and Kaucuk Group a.s. under government-held holding company Unipetrol a.s.
The government subsequently sold a 49 percent stake to the foreign consortium at the end of 1995 for $173 million.
Chemopetrol and Kaucuk will also be merged into Unipetrol on July 1. The holding company should be listed on the Prague Stock Exchange in September.
